name: Mighty Networks
tagline: Community, course, membership, and event platform for creators

pricing.notes: Official site checked 2026-07-30; Launch plan shown at $950/year, equivalent to about $79.17/month; monthly billing may differ.

tiers.name: Launch
tiers.limits: Unlimited members and spaces; 3 hosts; 10 moderators; 200 GB storage; 20 streaming hours/month; 100 viewers/stream; 5 profile fields; 1 landing page; 2 scheduled promotions; 2% transaction fee
tiers.notes: $79/month when paid annually; $95 month-to-month. The separate pricing calculator rounds the annual investment to $950/year.

tiers.name: Scale
tiers.limits: Unlimited members/spaces; 5 hosts; 15 moderators; 500 GB; 30 streaming hours/month; 200 viewers/stream; 10 profile fields; 1 landing page; 5 promotions; 5,000 Admin API calls/month; 1% transaction fee
tiers.notes: $179/month when paid annually; $215 month-to-month; annual investment shown as $2,150/year.

tiers.name: Growth
tiers.limits: Growth support, advanced automations and AI; numeric platform limits were not fully exposed on the public Growth page
tiers.notes: $4,250/year, billed annually; no public month-to-month option verified.

tiers.name: Mighty Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited hosts/moderators; 4 TB storage; 50 streaming hours/month; 3,000 viewers/stream; 10 landing pages; 15 promotions; 0.5% transaction fee

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; 14-day Growth-plan trial with no credit card
pricing.billingTerms: Launch and Scale monthly + annual (2 months free annually); Growth annual only; Mighty Pro custom
pricing.hiddenCosts: Transaction fees of 2%/1%/0.5% are added to payment processing. Extra storage, livestream hours and participant capacity use paid Engagement Boosts; up to 10,000 livestream viewers costs extra. Branded apps, SSO, email white-labeling, strategy, community management and advanced reports are optional paid additions.

verdictSummary: A private community/course site is possible, but Mighty sells the integrated community, payments, events, AI setup, mobile, and branded-app path.
coreLoopDIY: Build or self-host community software, gate access with payments, add courses/events, and send notifications.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because successful communities require ongoing admin, engagement, and mobile access.

priorArt.desc: Open-source community platform; can replace discussion/community parts but not every creat

alternatives.desc: Courses, forums, events, badges and paid enrolment are all here; the creator-brand gloss emphatically is not.

rejectedAlternatives.name: HumHub
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A capable community and event hub, minus the course-selling and subscription machinery.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Odoo Community
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Its modules cover the nouns, but the result is an ERP portal rather than a membership community.

notes: Useful community comparison; not a no because open-source can cover the core forum.
prompt:
Build me a small paid-membership community site to replace Mighty Networks. Requirements:

- Node + Express + better-sqlite3 on my VPS behind a reverse proxy, server-rendered
  pages, no frontend framework. Built for a community of dozens, not thousands;
  note in the README that self-hosted Discourse is the heavyweight alternative.
- Stripe subscription (keys in .env) gates membership: a webhook activates access
  on payment and revokes it on cancellation. Sign-in by emailed magic link, no
  passwords.
- One chronological feed of member posts (Markdown, images to an uploads/ folder)
  with threaded comments and like counts.
- An events page: title, date, location or call link, RSVP list of member names.
- A weekly digest email of new posts and upcoming events via Resend or SMTP (creds
  in .env), with one-click digest unsubscribe.
- Admin page for my account only: remove posts, comp memberships, member list with
  payment status.
- All member data in one SQLite file. No analytics, no telemetry.
- Out of scope: mobile apps, courses, live streaming, and algorithmic discovery
  feeds. Chronological posts from paying members is the product.
- README: Stripe webhook setup, .env keys, and backup steps for the DB plus
  uploads folder.
